context:
Goal: stop the stray-branch prompt on "Push the merged lane head", which you saw recur over the past 36 h.
Problem (rule): the fix narrows your ruling 206 a, so it needs your word.
Based on (ruling): item 206 a (2026-11-03): a push that names no destination (`git push origin HEAD`) asks when the branch's own name differs from the branch it tracks; the measured harm was a new stray branch on GitHub.
Based on (measured): a branch `lane-x` that tracks `origin/batch-1` asks on `git push origin HEAD` whether or not `origin/lane-x` exists; `git push origin HEAD:lane-x` passes (lane probe on main's guard, 11:09 CST Nov 8).
Based on (notes): the prompt you saw is most likely such a push to the lane's own PR branch; this is unconfirmed until a Mac session reads the guard log near 11:00 CST.
Departs from: main, where every such push asks — the push asks only when the branch does not exist on GitHub yet.
Meanwhile: the lane finishes another fix and holds this one until you answer. Either way, the prompt's remedy will name `git push origin HEAD:<branch>`.

options.gain: No prompt when a lane pushes to its own existing PR branch.
options.how: The guard reads the local copy of the remote's branch list once per such push, and asks only when the branch is not there yet.
options.label: Skip existing branches
options.lose: Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo. A push to an existing branch that happens to share the local name passes with no prompt, so it could add commits to another lane's branch.

options.gain: No change to your ruling; every off-upstream push still asks, and sessions learn the quiet form.
options.how: Ruling 206 a stays; the prompt's remedy names `git push origin HEAD:<branch>`, so a session switches to that form, which never asks.
options.label: Keep the prompt; fix its text only
options.lose: You still see the prompt about once per session before the session switches forms.

ref: your ask ask-mw8321blnx; decision plain-push-asks (ruling 206 a); step stray-push-ask-source
reply: 11:49 CST Nov 8: a stands as your ruling, routed to lane push-head-upstream-name. It narrows 206 a, so the push stays quiet when the branch already exists on GitHub. On your note: 'quiet regardless' would also drop the prompt for a push that makes a new branch on GitHub. That is the stray-branch harm 206 a was made for. The lane builds a only. To also drop the new-branch prompt, say so here or in that lane, and it becomes a new question.
title: Should the stray-branch push prompt stay quiet when the branch already exists on GitHub?
